meta.about: T-SQL contract cases (HD-054). Each line after this one is a case: it pins what Fabric Desktop does with the SQL on this PC (local: the static check, Format SQL, and running it here or refusing to) and states what Fabric is expected to do (fabric). verification stays local_pinned until a live run against a dedicated test workspace confirms the fabric half; then it becomes verified_against_fabric with a verified block. See docs/live-testing.md.

sql: SELECT TOP 3 n FROM (VALUES (1), (2), (3), (4)) AS v(n) ORDER BY n

equivalent.sql: SELECT n FROM VALUES (1), (2), (3), (4) AS v(n) ORDER BY n LIMIT 3

sql: SELECT TOP 3 n FROM (VALUES (1), (2), (3), (4)) AS v(n) ORDER BY n
SELECT TOP 3 n FROM (VALUES (1), (2), (3), (4)) AS v(n) ORDER BY n
SELECT TOP (2) WITH TIES n FROM (VALUES (1), (2), (2), (3)) AS v(n) ORDER BY n

fabric.why: TOP WITH TIES isn't named on the Fabric T-SQL surface area page either way.

sql: SELECT TOP 50 PERCENT n FROM (VALUES (1), (2), (3), (4)) AS v(n) ORDER BY n

fabric.why: TOP PERCENT isn't named on the Fabric T-SQL surface area page either way.

sql: SELECT n FROM (VALUES (1), (2), (3), (4)) AS v(n) ORDER BY n OFFSET 1 ROWS FETCH NEXT 2 ROWS ONLY

equivalent.sql: SELECT n FROM VALUES (1), (2), (3), (4) AS v(n) ORDER BY n LIMIT 2 OFFSET 1

sql: SELECT n FROM (VALUES (1), (2)) AS v(n) ORDER BY n LIMIT 1

fabric.why: LIMIT isn't T-SQL.

xfail.format_keeps_findings: Format SQL rewrites LIMIT 1 into TOP 1 for a T-SQL target, so the SYN-001 error disappears after formatting; Format SQL should only change layout.

sql: SELECT TOP 3 n FROM VALUES (1), (2), (3), (4) AS v(n) ORDER BY n

fabric.why: TOP isn't Spark SQL.

sql: SELECT CAST('42' AS int) AS x

equivalent.sql: SELECT CAST('42' AS INT) AS x

sql: SELECT CONVERT(varchar(8), CAST('2024-03-05' AS date), 112) AS x
SELECT TRY_CAST('abc' AS int) AS x

equivalent.sql: SELECT try_cast('abc' AS INT) AS x

sql: SELECT TRY_CONVERT(int, 'abc') AS x
SELECT 7 / 2 AS x
known_difference: T-SQL divides two integers as integers (3); Spark SQL returns 3.5. SEM-003 warns.

sql: SELECT CAST(7 AS decimal(5,2)) / 2 AS x
SELECT CAST(42 AS STRING) AS x

fabric.why: STRING is a Spark type; T-SQL has no type called STRING.

xfail.check: The check doesn't flag CAST(... AS STRING) for T-SQL targets, though STRING isn't a T-SQL type.

sql: CREATE TABLE dbo.t (ts datetime2(7))

fabric.why: Warehouse tables keep at most 6 digits of seconds.

sql: CREATE TABLE dbo.t (amount money)

fabric.why: money isn't a Warehouse table type.

sql: SELECT DATEADD(day, 7, CAST('2024-02-25' AS date)) AS x

xfail.equivalent: Spark's date_add returns a date; on this PC the DuckDB translation (date + INTERVAL 7 DAY) returns a timestamp, 2024-03-03 00:00:00.

sql: SELECT DATEDIFF(day, '2024-01-01', '2024-03-01') AS x
note: Spark's datediff takes (end, start); T-SQL's takes (unit, start, end).

sql: SELECT EOMONTH(CAST('2024-02-10' AS date)) AS x
SELECT DATEPART(quarter, CAST('2024-08-15' AS date)) AS x
SELECT DATEFROMPARTS(2024, 2, 29) AS x
SELECT DATETRUNC(month, CAST('2024-08-15' AS date)) AS x

fabric.why: DATETRUNC is SQL Server 2022 T-SQL; the Fabric surface area page doesn't name it.

xfail.equivalent: Spark's trunc(date, 'MM') fails on this PC: DuckDB says the extract specifier "MM" isn't recognized.

sql: SELECT DATENAME(month, CAST('2024-08-15' AS date)) AS x

xfail.format_outcome: Format SQL crashes (AttributeError: 'tuple' object has no attribute 'strip' in sql_format._difference) instead of formatting or leaving the query alone.

sql: SELECT GETDATE() AS now

fabric.why: Accepted; the value changes each run, so rows aren't compared.

sql: SELECT FORMAT(CAST('2024-08-15' AS date), 'yyyy-MM') AS x

fabric.why: FORMAT isn't named on the Fabric T-SQL surface area page either way.

sql: SELECT CONCAT('a', NULL, 'b') AS x
known_difference: T-SQL CONCAT treats NULL as empty text ('ab'); Spark's concat returns NULL. No rule warns.

sql: SELECT 'a' + 'b' AS x
SELECT LEN('abc  ') AS x
known_difference: T-SQL LEN ignores trailing spaces (3); Spark's length counts them (5). No rule warns.

sql: SELECT CHARINDEX('b', 'abc') AS x
SELECT SUBSTRING('abcdef', 2, 3) AS x
SELECT TRIM('  ab  ') AS x
SELECT UPPER(REPLACE('a-b', '-', '_')) AS x
SELECT LEFT('abcdef', 2) AS l, RIGHT('abcdef', 2) AS r

equivalent.sql: SELECT left('abcdef', 2) AS l, right('abcdef', 2) AS r

sql: SELECT STRING_AGG(s, ',') WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY s) AS x FROM (VALUES ('b'), ('a')) AS v(s)

equivalent.sql: SELECT array_join(sort_array(collect_list(s)), ',') AS x FROM VALUES ('b'), ('a') AS v(s)

fabric.why: STRING_AGG is T-SQL; WITHIN GROUP ordering isn't named on the Fabric surface area page.

sql: SELECT CASE WHEN 'abc' = 'ABC' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS same

equivalent.sql: SELECT CASE WHEN 'abc' = 'ABC' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS same

fabric.why: Warehouse's default collation is case-sensitive.

sql: SELECT ISNULL(NULL, 5) AS x
SELECT COALESCE(NULL, NULL, 3) AS x
SELECT NULLIF(1, 1) AS x
SELECT IIF(1 > 0, 'y', 'n') AS x
SELECT NVL(NULL, 5) AS x

fabric.why: NVL isn't a T-SQL function.

sql: SELECT ISNULL(NULL, 5) AS x

fabric.why: Spark's isnull takes one argument.

sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS c FROM (VALUES (1), (NULL)) AS v(n) WHERE n = NULL

equivalent.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS c FROM VALUES (1), (NULL) AS v(n) WHERE n = NULL

sql: WITH s AS (SELECT n FROM (VALUES (1), (2), (3)) AS v(n)) SELECT SUM(n) AS total FROM s

equivalent.sql: WITH s AS (SELECT n FROM VALUES (1), (2), (3) AS v(n)) SELECT SUM(n) AS total FROM s

sql: WITH a AS (SELECT 1 AS n), b AS (SELECT n + 1 AS n FROM a) SELECT n FROM b

equivalent.sql: WITH a AS (SELECT 1 AS n), b AS (SELECT n + 1 AS n FROM a) SELECT n FROM b

sql: WITH r AS (SELECT 1 AS n UNION ALL SELECT n + 1 FROM r WHERE n < 3) SELECT n FROM r

fabric.why: Microsoft documents recursive queries as unsupported.

sql: WITH RECURSIVE r AS (SELECT 1 AS n UNION ALL SELECT n + 1 FROM r WHERE n < 3) SELECT n FROM r

fabric.why: Apache Spark 3.5 has no recursive CTE; Fabric's runtime may differ.

known_difference: Runs on this PC (DuckDB has WITH RECURSIVE); Spark 3.5 doesn't document it. DML-002 is unverified.

sql: WITH a AS (WITH b AS (SELECT 1 AS n) SELECT n FROM b) SELECT n FROM a

fabric.why: Nested CTEs are in preview.

sql: SELECT n, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY n DESC) AS rn FROM (VALUES (1), (2), (3)) AS v(n) ORDER BY n

equivalent.sql: SELECT n, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY n DESC) AS rn FROM VALUES (1), (2), (3) AS v(n) ORDER BY n

sql: SELECT n, SUM(n) OVER (ORDER BY n ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS running FROM (VALUES (1), (2), (3)) AS v(n) ORDER BY n

equivalent.sql: SELECT n, SUM(n) OVER (ORDER BY n ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS running FROM VALUES (1), (2), (3) AS v(n) ORDER BY n

sql: SELECT n, LAG(n) OVER (ORDER BY n) AS prev FROM (VALUES (1), (2), (3)) AS v(n) ORDER BY n

equivalent.sql: SELECT n, LAG(n) OVER (ORDER BY n) AS prev FROM VALUES (1), (2), (3) AS v(n) ORDER BY n

sql: SELECT n, NTILE(2) OVER (ORDER BY n) AS b FROM (VALUES (1), (2), (3), (4)) AS v(n) ORDER BY n

equivalent.sql: SELECT n, NTILE(2) OVER (ORDER BY n) AS b FROM VALUES (1), (2), (3), (4) AS v(n) ORDER BY n

sql: SELECT g, n, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY g ORDER BY n) AS r FROM (VALUES ('a', 1), ('a', 1), ('a', 2), ('b', 5)) AS v(g, n) ORDER BY g, n

equivalent.sql: SELECT g, n, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY g ORDER BY n) AS r FROM VALUES ('a', 1), ('a', 1), ('a', 2), ('b', 5) AS v(g, n) ORDER BY g, n

sql: SELECT n FROM (VALUES (1), (2)) AS v(n) QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY n) = 1

fabric.why: QUALIFY isn't T-SQL.

xfail.check: The check doesn't flag QUALIFY for T-SQL targets; it isn't T-SQL.

sql: MERGE dbo.target AS t USING dbo.source AS s ON t.id = s.id WHEN MATCHED THEN UPDATE SET t.v = s.v WHEN NOT MATCHED THEN INSERT (id, v) VALUES (s.id, s.v);

fabric.why: Writes, so the live job never runs it; MERGE availability in Warehouse is checked by hand.

sql: MERGE dbo.target AS t USING dbo.source AS s ON t.id = s.id WHEN MATCHED THEN UPDATE SET t.v = s.v;

fabric.why: The SQL analytics endpoint is read-only.

sql: INSERT INTO dbo.t (id) VALUES (1)

fabric.why: The SQL analytics endpoint is read-only.

sql: SELECT * INTO dbo.copy FROM dbo.t

fabric.why: SELECT INTO creates a table; the endpoint is read-only.

sql: CREATE TRIGGER trg ON dbo.t AFTER INSERT AS SELECT 1

fabric.why: Triggers aren't supported.

sql: CREATE SEQUENCE dbo.seq START WITH 1

fabric.why: Sequences aren't supported.

sql: SELECT n FROM (VALUES (1)) AS v(n) FOR XML PATH('')

fabric.why: FOR XML isn't supported.

sql: CREATE TABLE dbo.t (id int PRIMARY KEY)

fabric.why: Keys must be NONCLUSTERED and NOT ENFORCED.

sql: CREATE TABLE dbo.t (id int, total AS id * 2)

fabric.why: Computed columns aren't supported.

sql: CREATE UNIQUE INDEX ix ON dbo.t (id)

fabric.why: Unique indexes aren't supported.

sql: CREATE TABLE ##g (id int)

fabric.why: ## global temp tables aren't supported.

sql: CREATE USER bob WITHOUT LOGIN

fabric.why: CREATE USER isn't supported.

sql: SET TRANSACTION ISOLATION LEVEL READ COMMITTED

fabric.why: Microsoft says the level can't be changed; whether the statement errors or is ignored isn't stated.

sql: BEGIN TRAN; SAVE TRANSACTION s1; COMMIT

fabric.why: Savepoints aren't supported.

sql: SELECT n FROM `v`

fabric.why: Backticks aren't T-SQL.

sql: EXECUTE AS USER = 'bob'

fabric.why: EXECUTE AS isn't supported in Fabric SQL database.
